source_review.notes: Checked the original Schmidt/O'Ryan/Kircher/Pyarali Leader/Followers paper, POSA2 and Reactor foundation; current POSIX condition-variable and mutex-lifecycle specifications; current Linux epoll/select manual semantics; RFC 9293; and the cited network, concurrency and performance texts. Demultiplexer, wakeup, cancellation, priority, close/reuse and affinity claims are scoped to exact platform verification.

evidence: Checked thread-set role partition, leader cardinality, handle-set/pool generation, active-handle claim, leader-gap, promotion latency and capacity notation.
Confirmed all set cardinalities, disjoint-union notation and role transitions use consistent meanings.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical leadership, actual scheduler execution, event selection, handler processing and durable external effect remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed the six-thread scenario: five processors plus one leader leaves zero followers; if the leader processes, all six are processors and leader count is zero.
Reproduced three-thread trace with one leader initially, successive t1-to-t2, t2-to-t3 and t3-to-t1 promotions, duplicate h1 exclusion and complete role accounting.
Confirmed each observed trace point has at most one leader and no more than one active entry per handle.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No real arrival rate, handler distribution, thread scheduling, promotion latency, cache effect, kernel backlog or platform performance was measured.

evidence: Verified monitor-protected absence/designation plus predicate recheck gives at-most-one abstract leader under the stated mutation assumptions.
Verified promotion-before-processing plus an eligible eventually scheduled successor gives conditional wait continuity.
Verified generation-qualified handle claim and current-generation reactivation exclude modeled duplicate processing and stale rearm.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: These conditional arguments do not prove scheduler fairness, OS/runtime correctness, lock implementation, thread survival, performance or multi-process ownership.

evidence: Reviewed initial/no-leader join, spurious/broadcast wake, simultaneous promotion attempts, no follower, delayed/dead successor, timeout/error/exception and cancellation while leader/follower/processor.

Reviewed level/edge/one-shot readiness, same-handle reselection, stream framing, close/descriptor reuse, unbound/bound affinity, multiple handle sets, priority inversion/starvation and nested dispatch.

Reviewed all-processors exhaustion, hidden kernel/upstream backlog, malicious slow work, reverse dependencies, staged shutdown, rolling generation transfer, rail control and air-traffic telemetry cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Exact event APIs, schedulers, real-time guarantees, security controls and safety domains require deployed integration/fault evidence and named human review.

evidence: Traced leader uniqueness, successor establishment, role partition, serialized handle claim, generation-safe reactivation, failure cleanup, capacity, priority and shutdown through exposition/examples/answers.
Checked executable trace retains exactly one leader through all modeled promotions, blocks duplicate h1, returns processors to followers and ends with no active handles.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite model omits locks, conditions, spurious wakeups, actual threads, event APIs, cancellation, failure, priority, timing, kernel queues and external effects and is labeled accordingly.

evidence: Reviewed leader-uniqueness argument against every assumed state mutation and wake predicate.
Reviewed continuity argument and its explicit eligible-follower/scheduler premises rather than claiming unconditional liveness.
Reviewed per-handle generation safety and capacity argument distinguishing bounded processors from unbounded external backlog.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof of a concrete monitor, demultiplexer, scheduler, network, distributed effect, security property or safety system is claimed.

evidence: Audited exactly one, at most one, continuous, atomic, safe, bounded, liveness, affinity, priority, performance, guarantee, proof and conclusion language.
Confirmed abstract protocol guarantees are conditional and cache/context-switch/latency claims are explicitly empirical and workload-specific.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Platform/version/configuration dependence is stated for demultiplexing, wakeups, cancellation, close/reuse, priority, affinity and shutdown.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/SEPAT-074/report.json
Reproduced deterministic role rotation, successor choice, duplicate-handle exclusion, processor rejoin, active-handle cleanup, leader cardinality and role partition using Python 3.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes one finite in-memory schedule only.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes rotating leader/follower/processor roles from a permanent Reactor dispatcher, generic thread pool and Half-Sync/Half-Async handoff, while preserving event and handle semantics.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers join/promotion predicates, deactivation/generation, failure cleanup, variants, hidden queueing, bounded handlers, ordering/reentrancy, security, shutdown, observability and platform verification.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with role and safety arguments, a runnable rotation trace, ten distinct examples and five complete exercises progressing from participant modeling through pool exhaustion, priority-aware multi-source design, diagnosis and rail-control transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
